title: STRESS BIOLOGY LAB
text:
STRESS BIOLOGY LAB


Department of Plant Science | School of Biological Sciences Central University of Kerala









About the Lab


SBL focuses on understanding plant physiology, stress responses, and the molecular mechanisms underlying plant growth, development, and adaptation to environmental challenges. Our research encompasses both biotic and abiotic stresses, with a major emphasis on endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, ER stress-induced programmed cell death (PCD), and ER-associated degradation (ERAD), which play crucial roles in maintaining cellular homeostasis and regulating plant stress responses. Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) serves as a major model for investigating ER stress signaling and associated cell death pathways, complemented by research using Arabidopsis thaliana, Nicotiana species, and Lathyrus species.


We integrate plant physiology, molecular biology, genomics, proteomics, and genome-editing approaches to investigate stress-responsive pathways and uncover the regulatory networks governing cellular homeostasis, stress signaling, and plant resilience. Our research aims to elucidate the molecular interplay between ER stress, protein quality control, and programmed cell death, while also exploring the mechanisms underlying plant responses to diverse environmental stresses and their potential applications in crop improvement and sustainable agriculture.

title: Research
text:
Overview


SBL focuses on understanding plant responses to environmental stress, with a particular emphasis on endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and their role in maintaining cellular homeostasis and survival under stress conditions.









1. ER Stress and Unfolded Protein Response (UPR)


We investigate how the accumulation of unfolded or misfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) activates the unfolded protein responses (UPR). Our research focuses on ER stress signalling, transcriptional regulation, and adaptive mechanisms that restore protein homeostasis and promote plant survival under stress.







2. ER-Associated Degradation (ERAD)


We study ER-associated degradation (ERAD), a protein quality-control pathway that recognizes selected misfolded or aberrant proteins in the ER and targets them for degradation, primarily through the ubiquitin–proteasome system. Our research aims to understand how ERAD maintains cellular homeostasis and contributes to plant stress adaptation.







3. Regulated IRE1-Dependent Decay (RIDD)


We explore regulated IRE1-dependent decay (RIDD), an RNA degradation process mediated by the endoribonuclease activity of IRE1. This pathway can regulate ER protein-folding demand and stress-responsive gene expression. We aim to understand its potential role in ER stress regulation and plant adaptation.







4. ER Stress-Induced Programmed Cell Death (PCD)


We investigate how prolonged or severe ER stress shifts cellular responses from adaptation toward programmed cell death (PCD). Our research examines the molecular regulators, signaling pathways, and cellular events associated with ER stress-induced PCD, aiming to understand their roles in plant development, stress responses, and survival.







5. Plant Stress Physiology, Molecular Biology, and Functional Genomics


We investigate plant responses to biotic and abiotic stresses, including heat, salinity, and drought, using physiological, biochemical, molecular, and omics-based approaches. By integrating genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and genome-editing strategies, we identify stress-responsive genes and regulatory networks and investigate their roles in plant adaptation, cellular homeostasis, and resilience.
